🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-08 23:00 → 2026-10-09 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Vectors PR #64 opened after PR #60 landed** — integrating the presence-test fix brought surviving edge cases down from 10 to 4 of 56, sharply narrowing the remaining implementation gap. [tg:tawg:5382]

> **Independent verification confirmed all vectors pass** — a second-opinion run on PR #64 validated 32/32 vectors and both presence and reachability controls, giving the group shared confidence before merge. [tg:tawg:5387]

> **Canonicalization facets drafted in a new ERC PR** — three open design points on pq_key_binding canonicalization moved from discussion into a reviewable spec proposal, separated cleanly from adjacent rules. [tg:tawg:5393]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### recompute-kit

_The implementation-to-verification relay on PR #64 closed a tight quality loop in one session._

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Completed** PR #60 in the ERC-8373 lane with a cold-clone run confirming 26/26 tests pass and the presence check catching all 13 expected cases, delivering the validated baseline that made the follow-on vector PR possible. [tg:tawg:5378]
- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Opened** PR #64 with updated vectors rebased on e4ed45e, cutting surviving edge cases from 10 to 4 of 56 and giving the group a much tighter target set to close. [tg:tawg:5382]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Verified** PR #64 independently at edbc5b6e, confirming 32/32 vectors and both presence and reachability controls pass under normal and optimized compilation, and classified the four remaining cases so reviewers know exactly what work is still open. [tg:tawg:5387]

### JCS canonicality

_A long-pending gist, a cost observation, and two quick prototypes moved this direction from backlog into active review in a single session._

- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Delivered** the JCS canonicality check gist Jimmy had requested in August, including a Solidity checker, providing a concrete implementation reference that immediately surfaced a real verification-cost question for the group to act on. [tg:tawg:5379]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Flagged** that the current approach carries high verification cost and proposed exploring a hash-based alternative, converting a latent efficiency concern into a clear design question the group could prototype against right away. [tg:tawg:5383]
- Baby Blue Viper **Built** the hash-based challenge Jimmy proposed and measured it against the five ERC-8373 statements pinned in recompute-kit, producing the first concrete cost data point for the proposed lower-cost path. [tg:tawg:5386]
- Baby Blue Viper **Shipped** a pinpoint version addressing the byte-violation state-dependence edge case, extending the prototype toward a more precise implementation that handles context-sensitive violations correctly. [tg:tawg:5390]
- Baby Blue Viper **Drafted** spec facet updates covering three open design points in a new ERC PR, framing pq_key_binding canonicalization as a distinct facet without touching adjacent rules, giving reviewers a targeted proposal to evaluate. [tg:tawg:5393]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Whether the four remaining survivor cases in PR #64 represent solvable edge conditions or choices worth encoding as explicit spec behavior
- How hash-based challenge cost compares to full JCS verification in representative workloads, now that initial measurement data exists
- Whether the new ERC PR's facet boundary placement aligns with the broader group's expectations on scope

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review and merge or iterate on PR #64 now that independent verification is complete
- Review Baby Blue Viper's new ERC PR on pq_key_binding canonicalization facets
- Continue the verification-cost design thread opened by Jimmy and prototyped by Baby Blue Viper

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A design question raised in one message became a working prototype measured against real statements before the session ended — the full loop from idea to data in just a few hours.
>
> When the group moves that fast, even the changelog has to sprint to keep up — don't slow down now! 🚀
